title: Physics — comprehensive review for the grades below 10 (Grade 7–9 program)
note: A grade-by-grade physics test covering the program of the grades below 10, at the depth of a solid school course. Foundational (prerequisite) items are the easy questions within each grade; the Maths & practical-skills section underpins all of it. Grade-10 / IGCSE content (lenses, refractive index, electromagnetic induction, half-life, redshift, specific heat, etc.) is deliberately left out.

topics.name: Maths & practical skills (underpin all of physics)

questions.text: Rearrange a simple formula: from speed = distance / time, make distance the subject.
Substitute numbers into a formula and give the answer with the correct unit.
Read a measurement accurately from a ruler, a measuring cylinder and a thermometer.
Read a line graph: what does the gradient (steepness) tell you, and what does a flat line mean?
Write a large and a small number in powers of ten (e.g. 3000 and 0.005).
Calculate the area of a rectangle and the volume of a box, with units.
Use a fraction, a decimal and a percentage in a simple calculation.
Name the basic physical quantities and their units: length, mass, time, temperature.
Name common measuring instruments and what each measures (ruler, balance, stopwatch, thermometer, measuring cylinder).
What is a force? Give examples (push/pull) and name several types (gravity, friction, magnetic, contact).
How is a force measured, in what unit, and with what instrument (newton, spring balance)?
Describe gravity as a force, and explain the difference between mass and weight.
Name several forms/stores of energy and describe one energy transfer.
State that energy is conserved, and that it tends to dissipate (spread out, become less useful).
What is density (mass per unit volume), and how would you measure the density of a stone?
Use the idea of density to explain why some objects float and others sink.
How is sound produced, and why can it not travel through a vacuum?
What causes an echo, and what changes the pitch and the loudness of a sound?
Describe electric current as a flow of charge/electrons; give an example of a conductor and an insulator.
Build a simple series circuit and draw the symbols for a cell, switch, lamp and ammeter.
Where is an ammeter connected, and what happens to the current when you add more lamps in series?
Calculate speed (speed = distance / time); what is meant by average speed?
Draw and interpret a distance–time graph (steady speed, faster, stationary).
Explain the difference between speed and velocity, and what acceleration means.
Describe the effect of balanced and unbalanced forces on motion, and the role of friction.
What is the turning effect of a force? Use moment = force × distance, with an example (seesaw/lever).
Define pressure (force / area); explain why skis or wide tyres reduce pressure on the ground.
Use the particle model to explain pressure in liquids and gases, and how it changes with depth.
What is atmospheric pressure, and give one piece of evidence that it exists.
Explain the difference between heat and temperature, and how a thermometer works.
Describe thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases, with an everyday example.
Describe conduction, convection and radiation, with an example and an application of each.
State that light travels in straight lines; explain how we are able to see objects.
State and use the law of reflection, and describe the image formed in a plane mirror.
Describe refraction (light bending) when it passes into glass or water, and why it happens.
What does a prism do to white light, and why does a coloured object look that colour?
Describe a magnet and its magnetic field, and say which materials are magnetic.
How do you make an electromagnet, how can you make it stronger, and give a use.
Define velocity and acceleration; interpret a speed–time graph (what its gradient and area mean).
State Newton's first law (inertia) with an example.
Use Newton's second law, F = m × a, in a simple calculation.
State Newton's third law with an example.
Define momentum (p = m × v), calculate it, and state the idea of conservation of momentum.
Describe gravitation as a universal attraction; what is free fall and the value of g?
Calculate work done (work = force × distance) and state its unit.
Calculate kinetic energy and the change in gravitational potential energy (m × g × h).
Define power (work / time) and efficiency, and do a simple calculation.
Explain upthrust (buoyancy), and relate floating to density and upthrust.
Define electric current, potential difference (voltage) and resistance, and state their units.
State and use Ohm's law (V = I × R) in a calculation.
Compare how current and voltage behave in series versus parallel circuits.
Calculate electrical power (P = V × I) and the energy used by an appliance.
Describe that an electric current produces a magnetic effect (electromagnetism) and give a use.
Define the amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period of a wave.
Explain the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves, with an example of each.
Use the wave equation, wave speed = frequency × wavelength, in a calculation.
Describe the properties of sound waves (reflection/echo, pitch ↔ frequency, loudness ↔ amplitude).
Describe the structure of the atom (nucleus of protons and neutrons, electrons around it); what are atomic number and mass number?
